findings.conditions: MatGetRowMaxAbs on an MPISBAIJ matrix with >=3 ranks; a low rank (e.g. rank 0, which only sends, eager MPI_Send) returns early and starts the next communication on the same PETSc inner communicator (another MatGetRowMaxAbs, a VecScatter/PetscSF of MatMult, etc.) before a higher rank has finished its receive loop
findings.reasoning: Rank r receives r messages with MPI_ANY_SOURCE and MPI_ANY_TAG on PetscObjectComm(A), which is the inner communicator shared by every PETSc object on that user communicator. Senders use tag=rank and blocking eager sends, and nothing synchronises before return, so rank 0 can be one or more operations ahead. The wildcard receive can then take a message from a later MatGetRowMaxAbs call (maybe for another matrix, giving wrong maxima, and the real message is then taken in the next call) or a scatter/assembly message with another tag and type. That gives wrong values, or MPI_ERR_TRUNCATE (abort) when the stolen message is longer than count, and the operation that lost its message can hang. The receive should name the source (source loop index) and a dedicated tag (PetscObjectGetNewTag).

findings.conditions: PCTFS used while the application, or another library, has point-to-point traffic on MPI_COMM_WORLD with tags in the MSGTAG range
findings.reasoning: PCTFS_giop/grop/giop_hc/grop_hc/ssgl_radd (lines 97,108,119,126,169,180,191,198,245,260,287,305,352,367) post blocking MPI_Recv with MPI_ANY_SOURCE on MPI_COMM_WORLD itself, not on a duplicated communicator, with fixed small tags (MSGTAGn + rank). Between PCTFS ranks the tag encodes the source, so the internal matching is deterministic. But any user message on MPI_COMM_WORLD with a colliding tag that is in flight can be taken in place of the partner's message, which corrupts the reduction and leaves the real message for a later receive.

findings.conditions: Multi-rank run; IDLE replies from the previous EvaluateFunction call are still in flight when the next call starts
findings.reasoning: The manager receives with MPI_ANY_SOURCE/MPI_ANY_TAG and counts IDLE messages without telling stale ones (left over from the previous evaluation's ping-pong) from fresh ones. Every worker has exactly one outstanding message, and results carry their task index as tag, so the protocol appears to stay consistent. Only the order of work assignment varies, so a real failure is unlikely. Listed for completeness.
